name: Postsecondary Planning for Students With Disabilities
title: Postsecondary Planning for Students With Disabilities
answer: Students with disabilities need postsecondary planning that prepares them for a different accommodations landscape, where colleges and employers expect students to request support on their own. AI can help students research disability services and compare documentation requirements, but self advocacy is the most important skill to build. The student and their team review any findings, and official college disability services information is the final source.

sections.body: Students with disabilities have planning needs beyond the general college and career process. Their transition plans should connect directly to their postsecondary goals. The key difference is that colleges and employers handle accommodations differently than schools do, and students usually have to request them without someone arranging it for them. Counselors and special education staff should help students prepare for that shift. This idea solves the problem of students arriving at college or work unprepared to navigate accommodations on their own.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: AI can support students as they research disability services at colleges and training programs. A student might use it to compare what documentation different colleges require or what supports they offer, then review the findings with their team and plan next steps. Self advocacy practice is central, and mock conversations with a school configured tool followed by discussion with a counselor can help students learn to describe their needs and request accommodations. The text does not give separate grade band guidance, so the work applies across the transition planning years. The goal is a student who can speak for themselves after high school.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no evidence label, study, or figure for this idea. It rests on practice and on the judgment of counselors and special education staff rather than on research findings stated in the book.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: Official information from each college's disability services office should be the final source, so AI research is a starting point and not an authority. The student and their team review findings together and decide next steps, which keeps the decisions with people rather than with the tool. Self advocacy practice through mock conversations is followed by discussion with a counselor, so a person guides the reflection. The aim is a student who can speak for themselves, which means the tool supports preparation but does not replace the student's own voice.
